title: Triode region and the MOSFET as a variable resistor

sections.heading: The idea
sections.body_md:
When \(V_{DS} < V_{ov}\), an inversion layer connects the source to the drain. At a point \(y\) along the channel, the local inversion charge is \(C_{ox}(V_{GS} - V(y) - V_T)\). The channel potential \(V(y)\) rises from 0 at the source to \(V_{DS}\) at the drain, so the channel gets thinner toward the drain.

Integrating the drift current \(I_D = \mu_nC_{ox}W(V_{GS} - V - V_T)\,dV/dy\) along the channel gives the triode equation. For very small \(V_{DS}\), the device is a plain resistor whose conductance is proportional to \(V_{ov}\), which is useful for switches and variable resistors. Digital logic gates spend much of their on-time in this region, and analog designers use triode devices as tunable resistors in filters and as current-source loads that are deliberately kept out of it.

sections.heading: Key equations
sections.body_md:
\[ I_D = \mu_nC_{ox}\frac WL\left(V_{ov} - \frac{V_{DS}}2\right)V_{DS} \]
\[ R_{on} \approx \frac{1}{\mu_nC_{ox}\frac WLV_{ov}} \quad (V_{DS} \ll V_{ov}) \]
The parabola reaches its peak at \(V_{DS} = V_{ov}\), where its value equals the saturation current.

sections.heading: Worked example
sections.body_md:
Take \(\mu_nC_{ox} = 200\ \mu\mathrm{A/V^2}\), \(W/L = 10\), \(V_{ov} = 0.5\ \mathrm{V}\) and \(V_{DS} = 0.1\ \mathrm{V}\):
\[ I_D = 2\ \mathrm{mA/V^2}\times(0.5 - 0.05)\times0.1 = 90\ \mu\mathrm{A} \]
The linear estimate \(2\ \mathrm{mA/V^2}\times0.5\times0.1 = 100\ \mu\mathrm{A}\) is 10% high. The small-\(V_{DS}\) resistance is \(R_{on} = 1/(2\ \mathrm{mA/V^2}\cdot0.5) = 1\ \mathrm{k\Omega}\).

sections.heading: Common pitfalls
sections.body_md:
- Using the triode formula when \(V_{DS} > V_{ov}\). Beyond the peak, the real device saturates instead of following the parabola back down.
- Dropping the \(V_{DS}/2\) term when \(V_{DS}\) is not small.
- In a switch, forgetting that \(V_{GS}\) falls as the signal voltage at the source rises.

sections.heading: Where this leads
sections.body_md: Setting \(V_{DS} = V_{ov}\) gives the square law, and what happens past that point is saturation.
